title: Searching in the Reassign lead technician dialog narrows the technician list
custom_preconds:
1. Sign in to the Work Orders build under test as a user whose role has Work Orders view and Work Orders create and edit. To check: Settings > Roles & Permissions > open the role > Work Orders (an Owner or Admin role has both).
  2. Use a desktop browser window at least 1024 px wide. Narrower windows show only the List, without the display switcher.
  3. In the top bar, pick the location you will test in (e.g. "Heavy Duty") and stay in it for the whole case.
  4. At least 3 technicians are eligible at this location (e.g. "Esther Howard", "Ralph Edwards", "Dana Ortiz"). A staff member is eligible when Clockable is on, the staff record is Active, the role is neither Office nor Time Clock User, and they are enrolled at this location. To add one:
    • Settings > Staff > add a staff member, enter a first and last name (e.g. "Dana Ortiz") and an email.
    • Pick a role that is not Office or Time Clock User (e.g. "Technician"), turn Clockable on, keep the record Active, enrol the staff member at this location, then Save.
  5. One staff member who must NOT be offered: an Office-role user (e.g. "Owen Office"). Create them the same way under Settings > Staff, but pick the Office role.
  6. Create a customer used only by this case so a search shows only its work orders: Customers > New Customer, name (e.g. "ZZ Board Test Co"), add an asset with a unit number and year/make/model (e.g. unit "TRK-118", "2022 Freightliner M2"), then Save.
  7. Create the work order: Work Orders > New Work Order > pick the case customer (e.g. "ZZ Board Test Co") and its asset > create it, and write down its number (e.g. "S1-702").
  8. On the work order page set Lead Technician to "Esther Howard".
  9. On the Lines tab click New Line, enter a name (e.g. "Brake inspection") and labor hours (e.g. 2.0), and save the line.
  10. Click the line's Approve (check) button so the work order status reads Approved.
custom_steps:
1. Open Work Orders, click the All tab and pick Board View in the display switcher (right side of the toolbar; in the design its button tooltip reads "Board").
  2. Type the case customer's name (e.g. "ZZ Board Test Co") in Search.
  3. Hover the work order's card (e.g. "S1-702") in Esther Howard's column and click its More actions (…) button.
  4. Choose Reassign lead technician.
  5. Read the top of the dialog and the list of choices.
  6. Click the dialog's search box (in the design it reads "Search technicians") and type Ral
  7. Clear the search box and type ral (all lower case).
  8. Clear the search box and type Owen
  9. Clear the search box and type zzqx
  10. Clear the search box.
  11. Click Cancel.
  12. Open the same card's More actions menu again and choose Reassign lead technician.
  13. Read the search box.
  14. Click Cancel.
  15. Pick Tech View in the display switcher and repeat steps 3 to 14 using the row's More actions (…) button.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 5: the dialog names the work order it is changing, by number and customer (in the design: "S1-702 · ZZ Board Test Co"), and marks Esther Howard as the current lead (the design highlights her with a check mark). Write down what you see; a different layout alone is not a fail.
  • Step 5: the list offers Unassigned and the eligible technicians of this location, e.g. Esther Howard, Ralph Edwards and Dana Ortiz.
  • Step 6: only technicians whose name contains "Ral" stay in the list: Ralph Edwards. Esther Howard and Dana Ortiz disappear from it.
  • Step 7: lower-case "ral" gives the same list, Ralph Edwards only. Upper or lower case does not matter.
  • Step 8: no technician is listed for "Owen". Owen Office has the Office role and is never offered, not even by searching.
  • Steps 8 and 9: when nothing matches, the dialog says so and repeats what you typed (in the design: No technicians match “zzqx”). Write down the words you see; a different wording alone is not a fail.
  • Step 10: clearing the search box brings back the whole list from step 5.
  • Step 11: nothing changes. The card stays in Esther Howard's column and no message appears.
  • Step 13: the search box is empty when the dialog opens again.
  • Step 15: Tech View behaves the same way, and the row stays in Esther Howard's group.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-10043; story SV-10047 (Story 4, Reassign or unassign the lead technician); PRD Confluence 845185030, edited 7 Oct 2026 (status line "PRD v33"), S4-R12, S4-R14 and section 8 "Design updates required from Branko" (Reassign dialog content and search), read 8 Oct 2026. Eligibility from PRD section 5 Terminology (Technician). Design export of 8 Oct 2026 (Branko Cicovic, Claude Design project 787fef1a, Work Orders.dc.html): Reassign dialog subtitle "work order number · customer" (assignSub, line 1363), search box "Search technicians" (line 357) keeping the technicians whose name contains the typed text in any letter case (lines 1180-1181), current lead highlighted with a check mark, no-match text "No technicians match “the typed text”" (line 1366), search emptied each time the dialog opens (openAssign, line 900). Design crawl 8 Oct 2026: Board View state 225 and Tech View state 193 ("S1-702 · Fibridge Commercial"), Board View states 227-228 ("No technicians match “Fib”", "No technicians match “zzqx-no-match”"). Design-only details (subtitle, search behaviour, no-match text, current-lead mark) are cited to the design; the PRD does not fix their wording. The list content (eligible technicians and Unassigned) follows S4-R12. Source-verified 8 October 2026; not yet build-verified.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S4-R12: “The dialog offers eligible active technicians in the current location and Unassigned.”
  • S4-R14: “Canceling the dialog leaves the lead unchanged.”
  • Design updates required from Branko: “Reassign dialog content, search, grouping, avatars, and exact “N open” count.”
